subject: The default prior for level-1 variance in a VC model

messages.author: 93e5626dd6dee825
messages.subject: The default prior for level-1 variance in a VC model
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to fit a VC model using:

    formula<-Y ~ 1 + f(iid, model="iid",
                     hyper=list(theta=list(prior="loggamma", param=c(1E-03,1E-03))))


    model<-inla(formula,
                   family="gaussian",
                   data=mydata,
                   quantiles=c(0.025,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.975))

and I would like to specify the prior, not only for the hyper parameter of the random effects, i.e. "iid" term, but also for the residual variance of the 
"gaussian" model. My question is if it is possible, and what is the default prior used for the residual variance by INLA??


Thanks,

--Ehsan

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The default prior for level-1 variance in a VC model

On Mon, 2016-02-01 at 00:28 -0800, Ehsan wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I am trying to fit a VC model using:
>
>     formula<-Y ~ 1 + f(iid, model="iid",
>                      hyper=list(theta=list(prior="loggamma",
> param=c(1E-03,1E-03))))
>
>
>     model<-inla(formula,
>                    family="gaussian",
>                    data=mydata,
>                    quantiles=c(0.025,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.975))
>
> and I would like to specify the prior, not only for the hyper
> parameter of the random effects, i.e. "iid" term, but also for the
> residual variance of the 
> "gaussian" model. My question is if it is possible, and what is the
> default prior used for the residual variance by INLA??

Hi, you can define the prior for the precision in the Gaussian responce
in the same way (see inla.doc("gaussian")), using the control.family
variable,

inla(...,

control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(
prior = "loggamma",
param = c(1, 0.0001))))


'prec', 'precision', 'theta' are all various names for the same
precision parameter (see the inla.doc(...)).


the Gamma(eps,eps) prior is know to be very bad, and its discussed for
example here

@Article{art460,
  author =       {Y. Fong and H. Rue and J. Wakefield},
  title =        {Bayesian inference for Generalized Linear Mixed
                  Models},
  journal =      {Biostatistics},
  year =         2010,
  volume =       11,
  number =       3,
  pages =        {397--412}
}


There is also a new concept of 'penalized complexity priors' which
suggest an exponential prior on the stdev scale. see http://arxiv.org/a
bs/1403.4630 and read v3 which is the better one.   this prior is avail
as  prior = "pc.prec", param = c(U, alpha), see inla.doc("pc.prec")
